doc.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Percussion setups for big band, conjunto and charanga; gig with Cugat's band
summary: He explains which percussion fits each ensemble type and recalls a gig with the Cugat band led by its pianist, which Victor got him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. That’s an LP, right? Xavier Cugat. I got the chance to perform with him too, with the group, but he wasn’t there, but the piano player was the leader. Me and Victor. Victor got me the gig. We did a gig with his band. But you see so now we’re starting to divide this thing up. Now for instance, big band for a percussionist, I’m a conga player, I’m expecting a bongo player, you’re going to see tonight, and a timbale player. That’s the full rhythm section of a big band. When you play cojunto, cojunto is only like maybe three trumpets, not like a big band, four four and four, or five, four and four, whatever. Cohunto is only four or three trumpets, it’s only a conga and bongo. Charanga it’s another style of music, three violins and a flute and that’s a conga and a timbale only. So those combinations you’ve got to know first of all. I’m not going to bring a pair of bongos to a charanga gig because there is no bongo. So see those are the things that we have to, you know, teach first in order to start — you know it’s not as black and white as it is. This is not what style you’re playing and who are you listening to. Who plays that style? What groups? Charanga Aragon — Aragon is like Cuba’s, like top charanga band, it’s been over 65 years you know. And this is the typical — charanga is the style of music of a cross between classical and it was like an upper class music because they had violins and flute but they put it into a cha cha cha and to a son montuno but you still had the violins. It’s more of a high society music, at the time. And they had danzones which is a French contra-dance, with classical music, but it went into a classical piece for the intro, then it goes into a son montuno a chacha, the body. And then the head out is the same as the head in, it finishes out in the classical setting.
